notes:
Summary: Orchid builds post-call intelligence for midsize contact centers (omnichannel). Evaluating Redwood for live agent-assist + post-call QA and automated ticket creation.

Recent timeline:
- 2024-11-03: Intro call (Jordan) — product fit looks strong; voiced concern around concurrent spike handling.
- 2024-11-15: Demo + live transcript walkthrough (Fireflies: ff-2024-11-15-orchid-poc-demo). Ran 10 sample calls; agent highlight extraction promising.
- 2024-11-29: SLO/capacity deep-dive with SE (Priya) — discussed 99th pct latency targets, fallback model routing and burst pools.
- 2024-12-02: Security questionnaire submitted by Orchid; Redwood provided initial answers and Drive doc.
- 2024-12-03: Onsite network/infra sync with Orchid infra lead — VPC peering window needs scheduling.

Use-case details / requirements (from PO + Dir. CX):
- Primary workload: post-call summaries -> generate bulletized transcript summaries + QA flags for supervisor review.
- Secondary: real-time agent assist (short prompts), tool-calling (open ticket in Zendesk via structured output).
- Volume: 1M calls/month projected after growth; peak concurrency 3-4k concurrent short calls/day.
- Latency targets: 95th pct summary <= 6s for short calls (<= 3min), real-time assist sub-300ms suggestion latency target for token completions.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit cost reduction >20%.
- Model preferences: open models preferred; willing to consider quantized variants. Need fallback to smaller/default model during spikes.
- Data residency: US-only for PII/voice logs; retention policy 90 days by default.

Security & compliance notes:
- Orchid requires SSO/SAML, audit logging for transcript access, and KMS integration for envelope encryption.
- Raised SOC2 + ISO27001 as must-haves for procurement. Redwood provided SOC2 summary doc; Orchid legal reviewing.

POC plan (agreed):
- 2024-12-09: Start 2-week POC (20k calls) against Dedicated pool w/ prefix caching enabled.
- POC success metrics: summary accuracy (human QA pass rate >= 85%), end-to-end latency targets met, structured ticket creation reliability >= 99%.
- Data flows: RTP transcripts -> Redwood ingest -> summary + QA flags -> Zendesk via webhook (sample mapping in Drive).

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need coachable highlights that our supervisors can action in seconds — not a 300-word blob." — Dir. CX, L. Ramirez
- "If the model slows during promo spikes, ops will be swamped. Fallback must be seamless." — Head of Ops, M. Chen

Open items / blockers:
- Final SOC2 artifact + ISO evidence (legal waiting).
- VPC peering scheduling with Orchid network team (they only provision windows on Thursdays).
- Confirmation of cost delta for reserved Dedicated pool vs burst pricing (finance).
- Transcript QA dataset: Orchid to supply 500 labeled calls for model calibration.

Next actions assigned:
- Jordan: send final POC contract + sample ingestion scripts (by 2024-12-06).
- Priya: produce config template for Dedicated pool + autoscale policy tuned for call spikes.
- Diego: coordinate CSM onboarding timeline assuming POC success.

Linked artifacts: Drive pricing deck, security FAQ, Fireflies transcripts.

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- Potential to upsell Optimize for batching suggestions and quantization recommendations if POC shows cost > target.
- Watch competitor Observe.AI demo scheduled next week — plant differentiation around fallbacks and KV prefix caching.

CRM-style shorthand:
- PO: L. Ramirez (Dir CX) — champion.
- Tech buyer: M. Chen (Head Ops) — worried about spikes.
- Legal: Karina V. — SOC2/ISO gate.
- "good fit" but procurement timeline depends on security artifacts and VPC window.
